text:
maria: Quick heads-up — sec review for the new private deploy template flagged two things we should triage: 1) egress rules in the sample NetworkPolicies are too permissive for the admin plane, and 2) RBAC role binding for the keystore operator grants cluster-admin in the example.

vikram: ack. Can you paste the offending snippets? I can propose tightened policies.

maria: pasted below. This is from “templates/priv-deploy/netpol-sample.yaml” in the repo:```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-admin-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: admin-plane
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - {}  # allows all egress
```

maria: and RBAC binding:```yaml
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: keystore-operator-crb
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: keystore-operator
  namespace: infra
```

ashley: yikes, granting cluster-admin by default is a no-go for private customers. We should have a minimal role and a hardened netpol.

tyler: agreed. For netpol we should list explicit CIDR/ports for KMS and control-plane only. e.g. egress to 10.0.0.0/16:443 and to 169.254.169.254 blocked, etc.

vikram: proposed fixes: 1) replace open egress with explicit rules to the KMS endpoints and internal service CIDRs; 2) change ClusterRoleBinding to a RoleBinding in infra namespace with only necessary verbs (get,create,update for secrets). I can open a PR.

maria: please do. Also add audit logging guidance: require kube-audit webhook enabled for private deploys and example rules that include resource:secrets, configmaps, and rolebindings. We need an auditable trail for keystore ops.

tyler: noted. One more thing: we found a vuln report (CVE-like) where an operator container can exec into host if PSP/PSP replacement isn't set. Make sure PodSecurity admission is enforced and we disallow hostPath and hostNetwork in the template.

vikram: good catch. I'll include a pod security yaml snippet and add automated checks in the deploy pipeline to fail on forbidden host* fields.

sec-bot: deploy-checker: New PR #482 by vikram will run the private-deploy policy gate: netpol, rbac, pod-security, audit-webhook.

maria: for incident response — if a private customer reports suspicious keystore activity, we should have runbooks for: 
- rotate KMS keys via customer KMS (we support AWS/GCP/Azure)
- snapshot audit logs and export to customer S3/GCS for legal hold
- optionally revoke service account tokens and fallback to read-only mode

ashley: do we have automation to rotate keystore encryption keys without downtime? Need to capture constraints (rolling restart of operator, rewrap secrets).

vikram: we support rewrap flows for AWS KMS and GCP KMS in the operator. I'll add a checklist: backup secrets, rewrap, restart operator, verify via sample read ops.

maria: thanks. Action items: @vikram open PR with tightened netpol + role change + podSecurity; @ashley doc runbook for keystore rotation + downtime constraints; @tyler add CI gate rule; sec team to add audit rule set to templates.

tyler: will add the CI gate today.

vikram: opening PR now — link will appear when ready.

sec-bot: pr-created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/482 by vikram :eyes:

maria: perfect. After PR lands, schedule a quick tabletop to run through the keystore rotate runbook (15 min).

ashley: ok, ping me for scheduling.

vikram: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/482 — includes netpol, role->rolebinding change, pod security, and audit webhook sample config.

maria: closing loop here — thanks all. We'll roll the template update behind a minor version and notify customers via the private-deploy changelog. :lock:
